# ruststream-rust-mqtt

> `ruststream-rust-mqtt` is the MQTT 5 broker crate for RustStream, a Rust framework for services that subscribe to message brokers and publish to them. It is built on the `rust-mqtt` client and serves two runtimes of RustStream: embassy, for a device that spawns the connection's runner as a task over its network stack, and compio, for a host where the broker starts the runner itself.

A subscription is a descriptor: `MqttTopic` for one topic, `MqttFilter` for a topic filter with wildcards, each with its own quality of service and share group. A service imports `ruststream_rust_mqtt::prelude::*`; a body that changes the quality of service or the retain flag of one message takes a step from `MqttPublishSteps`. `MqttBroker::new(config)` returns the broker with its `MqttRunner`, which owns the connection and has to run for the broker to connect. The in-process transport behind the `testing` feature lets the embedded and the compio `TestApp` run the production app without a server.

This site holds the guides, one page per component and the architecture of the crate; the API reference is on docs.rs, and the framework itself is documented on the RustStream site.

## Guides

- [Guides](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/): what the crate is and where to start
- [Getting started on a device](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/guides/getting-started-device/): the handler and the app, the runner task over the board's network stack, and the `start` that spawns both
- [Getting started on a compio host](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/guides/getting-started-compio/): `MqttBroker::compio`, which starts the runner on the core that connects the broker
- [Testing a device service](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/guides/testing/): the embedded and the compio `TestApp` on the production app, time moved by `advance`

## Components

- [Components](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/): the parts of the crate an MQTT service uses, one page each
- [MqttBroker](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/broker/): the broker and its runner, the three types of its lifecycle and the features of the crate
- [MqttConfig](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/broker/configuration/): the address, the client id, the keep-alive, the credentials and the persistent session
- [Network](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/broker/network/): the link the runner connects over, `EmbassyNetwork`, `CompioNetwork` and a network of the board's own
- [MqttTopic](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/subscriptions/): one topic with no wildcard, which answers for its own retry copies
- [MqttFilter](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/subscriptions/mqtt-filter/): a topic filter with the `+` and `#` wildcards
- [Qos](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/subscriptions/qos/): at most once, at least once or exactly once, and the level a delivery arrives at
- [Shared subscription](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/subscriptions/shared/): a share group, where the server hands each message to one member
- [One filter mounted twice](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/subscriptions/mounted-twice/): two handlers on one filter take the messages in turn
- [Acknowledgement](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/settlement/): what an `ack` and a `drop` send at each quality of service, and QoS 0
- [Negative acknowledgement](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/settlement/nack/): `retry` answers `Unsupported` and leaves the delivery unacknowledged
- [Retry after](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/settlement/retry-after/): a copy published after a delay, to the topic itself or to the topic the mount site names for a filter
- [MqttPublish](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/publishing/): the publish policy with its quality of service and retain flag
- [MqttPublishSteps](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/publishing/steps/): the `qos` and `retain` steps of one message
- [Retained messages](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/publishing/retained/): the last message of a topic, kept by the server
- [Headers and properties](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/publishing/headers/): typed headers as MQTT 5 user properties
- [The embedded TestApp](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/testing/): the embedded `TestApp`, the in-process server and its limits
- [Testing a compio service](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/testing/compio/): the compio `TestApp`
- [The live stand](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/components/testing/live/): a service against a real server, started by `just test-brokers`

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/architecture/): where the crate sits between the MQTT broker and the RustStream runtime
- [The runner and the handles](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/architecture/runner/): one task owns the connection, and the handles reach it through storage that exists from the start
- [What a delivery and a publish cost](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rust-mqtt/latest/architecture/cost/): the heap buffers of a delivery and the staging slot of a publish

## Reference

- [API reference](https://docs.rs/ruststream-rust-mqtt): the crate's rustdoc
- [RustStream](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream/latest/): the framework
